subject: Post-call: Veridian p95/p99 performance discovery & test plan
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@veridian.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 21 Jun 2026 21:12:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call: Veridian p95/p99 performance discovery & test plan

Thanks again for taking the time today — great discussion. Quick recap + concrete asks so we can move to an apples-to-apples run against your current provider.

Top-level goals (what Veridian told us):
- p95 end-to-end <= 180 ms for non-streaming completions (chat turn latency)
- p99 end-to-end <= 450 ms (hard target for SLA evaluation)
- Support streaming sessions (chunked token delivery) with incremental-latency < 80ms per token chunk under normal load
- Traffic envelope: steady-state ~600 req/s with peak bursts up to ~1200 req/s; streaming concurrency up to ~220 concurrent streaming sessions

What I attached: traffic_profile_v1.csv (per-minute RPS, token distribution), slo_acceptance_criteria.pdf (customer SLO doc).

Asks / next steps for Redwood team (can you confirm by EOD Monday?):
1) Can you run a 48-hour side-by-side run (same traffic profile) — Redwood hosted vs incumbent — and return p95/p99 end-to-end numbers, plus percentile breakdowns by request size? We want both streaming and non-streaming runs.
2) Please describe measurement definition (server-side vs end-to-end including network). Veridian will treat numbers as end-to-end (client observed).
3) Clarify any model variants you'd use for the test (quantized options, fp16, etc.) and whether warm caches will be enabled.
4) Call out any fallbacks/compatibility differences that could change tail (e.g., model truncation, tokenization differences).

Timing: Veridian asked for experimental results before their procurement kickoff on the 2nd week of July. Ideally we run the tests next week and deliver a short summary and raw samples.

Proposed quick plan: Ben to upload traffic profile (attached) -> Camila to confirm test harness and schedule -> run (48 hours) -> delivery of report + raw traces + perf artifacts.

Thanks — I can coordinate with your procurement contacts if needed.

Ben Carter
Senior Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@veridian.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@veridian.ai, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 09:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call: Veridian p95/p99 performance discovery & test plan

Thanks Ben — appreciate the clear recap. Quick clarifications from our side before you kick off testing: 

- Measurement definition: when we say "end-to-end" we mean client-observed (request injection point at our API gateway in us-east-1 to last byte delivered to the downstream client). Network hops inside our VPC are included; last-mile to end-user is not.
- p95/p99 targets above are what we'd like to see; procurement will expect to see a path to an SLA appendix with a p99 remedy.
- Pricing: procurement (cc'd) wants a ballpark on incremental cost to run with your hosted environment at our traffic envelope (we'll evaluate whether this is a capital or operational decision).

We can confirm the traffic_profile_v1.csv as representative. Two asks for Redwood before the run: 1) confirm which model variant and quantization you'll use for the test, and 2) confirm whether your measurements will include network egress/ingress latency on Redwood's side or if you'll provide server-side traces for us to correlate.

Can you also include a short note on warm-cache policy — e.g., will you run a warmup of X requests and keep a KV cache enabled during the run? That materially affects tail.

Alex
Head of Platform Engineering | Veridian
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@veridian.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 14:32:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call: Veridian p95/p99 performance discovery & test plan

Alex / Ben — thanks. Technical plan from Redwood (concise):

Planned test matrix (to be fair to incumbent):
- Baseline run: Veridian-provided incumbent endpoint (we'll replay same traffic against a passthrough harness to collect client-observed metrics).
- Redwood run: hosted API endpoints in us-east-1.
- Two modes: non-streaming (single completion) and streaming (chunk-size 50 tokens).

Measurement definitions / correlation: 
- We'll collect server-side traces (timestamped at ingress and egress of our runtime) and provide you both server-side and client-observed traces. We'll instrument with distributed trace ids so you can reconcile.
- By default we'll report client-observed numbers (to match your definition). Server-side numbers will be in the appendix.

Model / runtime settings we plan to use for the test: 
- Model: redwood-large-v1 (quantized INT8 profile) — same model family you tested previously with incumbent.
- Warmup: 10k synthetic requests (10 minute warmup ramp) to populate KV cache and kernel JIT paths. We'll keep KV cache enabled during the run to reflect production behavior.
- Prefetching/Batching: we'll run with continuous batching tuned to 100ms latency budget for the non-streaming workload. Streaming sessions will use per-session KV management; we will not artificially coalesce independent sessions.

Traffic harness and fairness knobs: 
- We'll run k6-based replay using your traffic_profile_v1.csv. Token distribution will match three buckets (short 1-64 tokens, medium 65-320, long 321-1024).
- Disable any incumbent-only prefix caching features on the baseline replay to reduce bias; we will note differences in the report.

Schedule & timing:
- We estimate a 48-hour run (12 hours baseline, 12 hours warmup/validation, 24 hours Redwood run) if we have a firm window.
- Cost estimate for the test: approx. $3,200 in hosting/test credits for the run (we'll provide a formal estimate in the report).

Action items for Alex / Veridian:
1) Confirm next available 48-hour window (target: week of 29 Jun).
2) Confirm whether procurement needs a draft SLA appendix prior to tests (we can provide a template).
3) Confirm whether the traffic CSV contains any PII — we'll need a signed test NDA if so.

I'll prepare the infra playbook and share the redwood-sim-harness-instructions.md link (attached).

— Camila Reyes
Performance Engineering | Redwood Inference
